Rashi on Menachot 87a:10:1.english: He would give it an extra hoeing - Meaning that he hoed it twice.

Rashi on Menachot 87a:10:2.hebrew: ודרי מיא על חד תרין - שהיה יכול למוזגו במים כפליים מיין אחר, דיין דעלמא דרי על חד תלתא, וזהו מקבל על חד ששה, והיינו על חד תרין דיין אחר:
Rashi on Menachot 87a:10:2.english: And it bears water at [a ratio of] one-to-two - Meaning, that it was possible to dilute it with water double [the amount] of other wine. For ordinary wine bears [dilution] at a ratio of one-to-three, and this one accepts one-to-six - and that is [what is meant by] "one-to-two [i.e., double] of other wine."

Rashi on Menachot 87a:11:1.english: Medium-sized jars of Lod - Medium-sized jars from Lod.

Rashi on Menachot 87a:12:1.english: One may not place the jars two [at a time] - meaning, one on top of another.

Rashi on Menachot 87a:17:1.hebrew: שגובהן כרחבן - שהיו רחבים מרוב שמנות, כמו שגבוהים, והיינו כר נרחב:
Rashi on Menachot 87a:17:1.english: That their height equals their width: That they were as wide as they were tall, from their abundant fatness - like a broad, spread-out cushion.

Rashi on Menachot 87a:18:2.english: They shall never be silent - [This refers to the Gemara's question:] What do these watchmen say?

Rashi on Menachot 87a:19:1.english: And initially - Before it [the Temple] was destroyed.

Rashi on Menachot 87a:19:2.hebrew: הוו אמרי כי בחר ה' בציון - אף לעתיד לבא, עתידים המלאכים להיות שומרים ולומר "כי בחר ה' בציון":
Rashi on Menachot 87a:19:2.english: They would say: “For the Lord has chosen Zion” - Even in the future to come, the angels will be destined to be watchmen and to say, “For the Lord has chosen Zion.”

Rashi on Menachot 87a:21:1.hebrew: שתי מדות - ר"מ אומר עשרון עשרון, דשני כלים היו שם, כל אחד מחזיק עשרון:
Rashi on Menachot 87a:21:1.english: Two measures - Rabbi Meir says [this alludes to the verse] "a tenth, a tenth," [which is written twice], for there were two vessels there, each one holding a tenth [of an ephah].

Rashi on Menachot 87a:22:1.hebrew: ולא היה מודד - לפר בכלי שמחזיק שלש עשרונות, אלא מודד שלש פעמים בעשרון:
Rashi on Menachot 87a:22:1.english: And he would not measure - [the meal-offering] for a bull in a vessel that holds three tenths; rather, he would measure three times with the [single] tenth [measure].

Rashi on Menachot 87a:24:1.english: One heaped - That it did not contain a [full] tenth unless it was heaped.

Rashi on Menachot 87a:24:2.english: And one leveled - That the leveled [vessel] was so large that when it was leveled off, it held a tenth [of an ephah].

Rashi on Menachot 87a:2:1.english: How does he check? - To know if the wine is good.

Rashi on Menachot 87a:2:2.english: This treasurer sits with a rod in his hand - and watches as this [rod] draws the wine out from the hole of the barrel.

Rashi on Menachot 87a:2:4.hebrew: הקיש - הגזבר על גבי הכד, וסותם זה מיד. וזה היה סימנו, שלא היה רוצה לדבר כל זמן שמוציאין היין:
Rashi on Menachot 87a:2:4.english: He knocked - [Meaning,] the treasurer [knocks] on top of the jug, and this one [who is drawing the wine] seals it immediately. And this was his sign, [used] because he did not want to speak the entire time that they were drawing out the wine.

Rashi on Menachot 87a:3:1.hebrew: שנאמר תמימים יהיו לכם - ואם היו בו קמחים, הוי כבעל מום:
Rashi on Menachot 87a:3:1.english: As it is stated: "They shall be unblemished for you" - and if it [the wine] had flour-like scum in it, it is considered like [an offering] with a blemish.

Rashi on Menachot 87a:5:1.hebrew: כרוך ותני - אין מביאין הליסטיון, לפי שאין מביאין לא מתוק וכו', ואם הביא פסול:
Rashi on Menachot 87a:5:1.english: Combine and teach - We do not bring the listion [wine], because we do not bring [wine that is] sweet, etc.; and if one did bring it, it is invalid.

Rashi on Menachot 87a:5:2.hebrew: רב אשי אמר - לא תכרוך, הליסטיון כשר דהויא חוליא דשמשא ולא מאיס, אבל מתוק מחמת הפירי מאיס, והיינו דקתני פסול:
Rashi on Menachot 87a:5:2.english: Rav Ashi said - Do not combine [the two clauses of the mishna into one], [for] the listron [wine from sun-dried grapes] is valid, since it is a cluster [that became sweet] from the sun, and that is not repulsive. But [wine] that is sweet because of the fruit itself is repulsive, and this is why [the second clause] teaches that it is invalid.

Rashi on Menachot 87a:7:1.hebrew: מאן שמעת ליה דאמר לא יביא רבי - דקתני במתניתין דברי רבי, והא ברייתא דקתני לא יביא [ע"כ רבי], וקתני (בהא ברייתא) אם הביא כשר, והיכי מ"ל ה"נ פסול:
Rashi on Menachot 87a:7:1.english: Whom did you hear say "he may not bring"? Rabbi - For it is taught in the Mishnah, "these are the words of Rabbi." And this baraita, which teaches "he may not bring" - that must perforce be Rabbi's view - also teaches (in this baraita), "if he brought it, it is valid." So how can you say that here too [i.e., wine, by analogy to a two-year-old lamb] it would be invalid?

Rashi on Menachot 87a:8:1.hebrew: היינו טעמא - שאין מביא ישן, דכתיב "אל תרא יין כי יתאדם", דלא הוה חשוב יין אלא אדום, ושנה ראשונה יש בו עיקר אדמומית, טפי לא, ולאו משום דלכבש דמי יין:
Rashi on Menachot 87a:8:1.english: This is the reason - that one does not bring old wine, as it is written: "Do not look at wine when it is red" (Proverbs 23:31) - meaning that wine was not considered [true] wine unless it was red. And only in its first year does it have its essential redness, no more than that - and this is not because wine is comparable to a lamb [i.e., not for the reason suggested earlier, that old wine is disqualified like a two-year-old lamb].

Tosafot on Menachot 87a:14:1.hebrew: כשם שהדיבור יפה לבשמים כו' - בפרק קמא דכריתות (דף ו:) קאמר רבי יוחנן איפכא גבי קטורת, דתני': כשהוא שוחק אומר "היטב הדק", וקאמר: מסייע ליה לרבי יוחנן דאמר: כשם שהדיבור רע ליין, כך דיבור יפה לבשמים. משום דכי קאמר רבי יוחנן בנסכים, קאמר להו כי היכי דקים לן בקטורת שהדיבור יפה לבשמים, כך הדיבור רע ליין; וכי קאי בקטורת, קאמר להו כי היכי דקים לן בנסכים שהדיבור רע ליין, כך הדיבור יפה לבשמים:
Tosafot on Menachot 87a:14:1.english: Just as speech is good for spices, etc. - In the first chapter of Keritot (6b) Rabbi Yochanan says the opposite regarding incense, for it was taught: while grinding it, one says, "Grind it well, grind it fine!" And [the Gemara] says: this supports Rabbi Yochanan, who said: just as speech is bad for wine, so speech is good for spices. [This is not a contradiction between the two statements,] because when Rabbi Yochanan said this regarding the wine libations, he said it precisely because it was already established for us, from the case of incense, that speech is good for spices - and from that he inferred that speech is likewise bad for wine. And when he was dealing with incense, he said it precisely because it was already established for us, from the case of the libations, that speech is bad for wine - and from that he inferred that speech is good for spices.

Tosafot on Menachot 87a:17:1.hebrew: שגובהן רחבים גרסינן, ולא שגובהן כרחבן, כדאשכחן רוחבו, מייתי קרא דכתיב כר נרחב. ובבראשית רבה אמר דכבשים של תמיד דהיו כל כך גבוהים שאוכלים על גבי ארזים, וכשהיו מרכיבין אותן על הגמלים רגלי הכבשים נגררין לארץ:
Tosafot on Menachot 87a:17:1.english: We have the reading "their height was vast [רחבים]" and not "their height was like their width [כרחבן]," just as we find the term "width" used [in this sense elsewhere] - it brings the verse that is written, "a vast pasture [כר נרחב]" (Isaiah 30:23). And in Bereishit Rabbah it says that the lambs of the daily offering were so tall that they would eat from atop cedars, and when they would load them onto camels, the lambs' legs would drag along the ground.

Tosafot on Menachot 87a:24:1.hebrew: אחד גדוש ואחד מחוק - תימה גדול, דר"מ דריש לה מקרא, דכתיב: "עשרון עשרון לכבש האחד", ובקונטרס פי' דר"מ ס"ל גמרא דשתי עשרונות בצבור:
Tosafot on Menachot 87a:24:1.english: One heaped and one level - This is a great wonder: Rabbi Meir derives this from a verse, since it is written, "a tenth, a tenth, for the one lamb" - yet Rashi explained that Rabbi Meir holds it to be a matter of received tradition (rather than a scriptural derivation) that two-tenths were used for communal [offerings].

Tosafot on Menachot 87a:25:1.hebrew: גדוש שבו היה מודד לכל המנחות - איפכא לא רצו לעשות למדוד בגדוש לחביתי כ"ג, שלא ישפוך הסלת לארץ כשחוצהו:
Tosafot on Menachot 87a:25:1.english: The heaped [measure] with which he would measure for all the meal offerings - They did not want to do the opposite: to measure with the heaped [measure] for the griddle-cakes of the High Priest, so that he should not spill the flour on the ground when he divides it [into two halves, for the morning and afternoon portions].
